# Builtin release 2: native content and verification limits

The manifest ships seven templates and five hooks. Bodies are compiled with embed; production builtin code imports only the core model/catalog and the standard library. It never imports render, reads installer media, or accesses a database. Tests build real snapshots and call the same Render entry for answers, menus, auxiliaries and execution wrappers. These tests establish deterministic text and selected Ubuntu shell behavior, not real installation success.

## Release and golden provenance

Kickstart and packages change from identity version1 to version2. New identities start at1. releases/v1.json and its two fingerprint files remain byte-identical. releases/v2.json is the complete current manifest, and each object has a SHA256 fingerprint of deterministic model JSON. PostgreSQL replay loads v1 then v2 twice and rereads every historical version, comparing both content and stored revision. Mismatched bytes under an existing identity/version remain rejected.

Raw historical file hashes (not model fingerprints):

- releases/v1.json: 266d3b6a7bce5488a6720ad17242beb0fc6b832a7ad8f3518c2f1eb798a382d3
- fingerprints/hook-builtin-packages-v1.sha256: 1b204804abe59133121329cd6b5e564f8360e0a92dd591c5ce13d60fa95587fa
- fingerprints/template-builtin-kickstart-v1.sha256: 8f8691e9f246b1c1aeaf3adde308ffc943ccb3f0515eb27966e170f7bff24991

The fourteen answers/ goldens were initially recorded only after activation, snapshot, native-contract, firmware, parameter and lifecycle assertions passed. The recording tests refuse to replace existing files. All BIOS/UEFI answer pairs are deliberately identical: the installer determines firmware; neither an optional registered Host.Firmware nor an independent operator default chooses disk layout. ESXi's BIOS answer file is only a deterministic rendering fixture; menu delivery rejects BIOS with firmware_mismatch.

Golden credentials, keys, URLs, product IDs and Windows image indexes are test fixtures. Production credentials have no default. Image index4 is not a claim that every Windows ISO has that image. Agama product SLES/Leap comes from the fixture ISO offer set; actual media IDs must come from the importer.

## Content sources and native decisions

| Format | Source and shipped decisions | Evidence and limits |
|---|---|---|
| Kickstart | [Red Hat command reference](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_enterprise_linux/9/html/automatically_installing_rhel/kickstart-commands-and-options-reference_rhel-installer), [upstream pykickstart](https://pykickstart.readthedocs.io/en/latest/kickstart-docs.html), [openEuler Kickstart](https://docs.openeuler.org/en/docs/21.09/docs/Installation/using-kickstart-for-automatic-installation.html). RHEL/Rocky/Alma/openEuler/OpenCloudOS share native Kickstart commands. Selected disk is wiped as GPT. A %pre hardware probe writes an include containing an ESP for UEFI or biosboot for BIOS, then /boot and root. Native user, sshkey, DHCP and package directives supply the other hooks. | Both emitted partition programs execute under Ubuntu bash and BusyBox sh with only the /sys/firmware/efi probe replaced. Assertions compare complete generated bytes and requested nvme0n1 selection. Native Anaconda versions and package-group availability on each actual ISO remain installer qualification. |
| Preseed | [Debian installation guide B.4](https://www.debian.org/releases/stable/amd64/apbs04.en.html), [partman source](https://salsa.debian.org/installer-team/partman-auto), [Debian UEFI](https://wiki.debian.org/UEFI). GPT plus native atomic proposal selects the installer’s BIOS or EFI recipe. Current recipes-amd64/atomic has method{ biosgrub }; recipes-amd64-efi/atomic has method{ efi }. The early command derives mirror transport/host/path from sys:repo. Native account/network/package answers precede late staging of the SSH hook. | Tests assert the configured proposal, disk, package list, lifecycle and derived URL shell fields. They do not execute partman or prove the selected media carries these recipes. Require a matching netboot installer, working package metadata and the appropriate native recipe. |
| Autoinstall | [Subiquity reference](https://canonical-subiquity.readthedocs-hosted.com/en/latest/reference/autoinstall-reference.html), [storage/boot behavior](https://canonical-subiquity.readthedocs-hosted.com/en/latest/howto/configure-storage.html). Direct GPT layout on the selected disk delegates boot-partition creation to Subiquity (BIOS boot area or ESP). Identity, SSH, DHCP netplan and package sections are native. Required template hostname also drives NoCloud meta-data. | YAML is parsed separately; Go tests assert proposal, values and consistent metadata. The body comment requires RAM exceeding the full ISO plus installer working memory, without adding a model/schema field. Curtin/Subiquity execution and actual ISO memory sizing remain layer7. |
| AutoYaST | [SUSE15 SP7 AutoYaST reference](https://documentation.suse.com/sles/15-SP7/html/SLES-all/cha-configuration-installation-options.html), especially expert partitioning, users and chroot scripts. AutoYaST adds missing boot partitions to the selected GPT disk/root proposal. Root is explicitly locked with encrypted !. Native authorized_keys is nested under the configured regular user; it is not raced against second-stage account creation. Native networking/packages and an outside-chroot script stage the existing Lober firstboot service. | XML parsing and nested-user assertions verify the data. Boot proposal execution, firewall policy, installer stage ordering and service startup on SLES15/Leap15 remain real-install checks. |
| Agama | [profile format](https://agama-project.github.io/docs/user/reference/profile), [storage](https://agama-project.github.io/docs/user/reference/profile/storage), [users](https://agama-project.github.io/docs/user/reference/profile/users), [network](https://agama-project.github.io/docs/user/reference/profile/network), [software](https://agama-project.github.io/docs/user/reference/profile/software), [hostname](https://agama-project.github.io/docs/user/reference/profile/hostname), [localization](https://agama-project.github.io/docs/user/reference/profile/localization), [scripts](https://agama-project.github.io/docs/user/reference/profile/scripts). Required enum product Offer=products has no default. Selected GPT disk deletes prior partitions and generates the product default volumes; boot.configure=true delegates boot requirements. One post chroot:false path stages systemd firstboot and SSH, with no scripts.init path. | Native Jsonnet0.21.0 evaluation and the pinned Agama v17 schema pass. [v17 release](https://agama-project.github.io/blog/2025/08/27/agama-17) discusses SLES16/Leap16, but that is not evidence every ISO ships this exact schema. Importer must identify and qualify the actual Agama build. |
| Unattend | [WinPE firmware probe](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/manufacture/desktop/boot-to-uefi-mode-or-legacy-bios-mode), [BIOS partitions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/manufacture/desktop/configure-biosmbr-based-hard-drive-partitions), [UEFI partitions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/manufacture/desktop/configure-uefigpt-based-hard-drive-partitions), [image metadata](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/customize/desktop/unattend/microsoft-windows-setup-imageinstall-osimage-installfrom-metadata), [AutoLogon](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/customize/desktop/unattend/microsoft-windows-shell-setup-autologon), [OpenSSH keys](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/openssh/openssh_keymanagement). Pre-hook reads PEFirmwareType. UEFI uses ESP260MiB/MSR16MiB/OS; BIOS uses a reserved recovery area750MiB/type27, active system550MiB, then OS. Both install to disk0/partition3. | XML and separate DiskPart branch structures are asserted on Ubuntu; no native Windows commands ran. Disk0 is pinned in both hook binding and InstallTo; deriving for another disk requires changing both. BIOS recovery space is reserved, not proof WinRE is configured; its early position differs from Microsoft's recommended trailing recovery partition and limits later growth. |
| ESXi ks | [VMware8 installation reference](https://d3bql97l1ytoxn.cloudfront.net/app_resources/447311/documentation/1439997_1721785831666_en-US.pdf), [ESXCLI software](https://developer.broadcom.com/xapis/esxcli-command-reference/latest/namespace/esxcli_software.html), [individual VIB installation](https://knowledge.broadcom.com/external/article/404699/install-individual-vibs-on-esxi-host.html). Native whole-disk firstdisk selection, DHCP and encrypted root password precede one encoded firstboot section. Packages means operator-supplied, individually qualified VIB URLs, not an ESXi system-upgrade depot. SSH is root-only. | BIOS is rejected at menu. Native firstboot requires Secure Boot disabled and the Task8 ABI/owned-$0 contract. Tests do not certify ESXi8/9 hash/base64/setsid applets, native persistence, driver compatibility or SSH backup lifecycle. |

Debian recipe bodies were inspected from the raw upstream [amd64 atomic](https://salsa.debian.org/installer-team/partman-auto/-/raw/master/recipes-amd64/atomic) and [amd64 EFI atomic](https://salsa.debian.org/installer-team/partman-auto/-/raw/master/recipes-amd64-efi/atomic) sources. Cached source SHA256 values are respectively `01a3995377c87d139fb9a2ca2fb484f02323f18444a56402a6a6653a3a1933b1` and `9bbe0d58e8ebeea11a3733707226de505693663e920e2c871bc89a1645ec8732`. The retrieval used master without recording an upstream commit; these source bytes establish the cited recipe contents, not their presence or version in an acceptance ISO.

Windows account and AutoLogon use the same supplied password in XML; the one short FirstLogonCommand chains firstboot, all configured hooks and cleanup with &&. Package features and SSH hooks read environment variables, never substituted command-source arguments. Feature reboots are deferred. The current UTF8 BusyBox/curl route requires qualification against both PE and the installed system; Server2016/2019 static edition coverage is explicitly not firstboot runtime support. SSH content guarantee is only Server2025; older systems require separate OpenSSH capability qualification. Real Windows ACL/API/Setup behavior remains layer7.

The shared compiled body `shared/linux-sshkey.sh` supplies the separate Preseed and Agama implementations without changing their series/timing metadata. Linux SSH scripts resolve the configured username with NSS, append the supplied key, set ownership/0700/0600 and restore security labels when available. Ubuntu tests replace only NSS lookup and verify actual file bytes and modes. Keep the SSH username equal to the account username in script-based formats. Native Ubuntu/AutoYaST SSH sections target the account they are nested under; their shared username declaration is unused. ESXi always binds root.

Native word restrictions protect syntax, not installer semantics. Interface names, usernames, disk names, package names, crypt schemes and feature IDs must still be valid for the selected media. The Linux packages hook appends packages; curl/systemd/SSH are separately mandatory. The ESXi packages hook enters maintenance mode, installs the provided VIBs, and exits maintenance only after success; a failure deliberately retains maintenance mode.

## Runtime and later layers

[The renderer runtime contract](../../../domain/render/testdata/runtime-contract.md) and [menu/aux contract](../../../domain/render/testdata/menu-aux-contract.md) remain authoritative.

- Layer4 provides immutable real media roles, actual edition/product offers, repository contents and helper ABI qualification. Linux installers need their native shell, HTTP fetch, base64 and hash tools; installed Linux needs curl, systemd, SSH and ordinary user/file tools. Package availability on the selected ISO/repository must be verified there.
- Layer5 invokes EnsureBuiltin hooks before templates, offers only current builtin identities, obtains parameters and calls activation/snapshot construction. There is no schema/model migration in this task.
- Layer7 checks actual firmware and Secure Boot before delivery, issues the independent finalize credential, serves only frozen digest payloads and runs real BIOS/UEFI installations. It validates installer stage order, boot partitions, networking/firewall, account/SSH behavior, native services, Windows helper compatibility and ESXi applets/$0 persistence. Neither golden files nor schema validation discharge these obligations.

## Reproducing the optional native parser checks

These are development checks outside the Go production dependency graph. No tool was installed globally. Jsonnet was executed with go run github.com/google/go-jsonnet/cmd/jsonnet@v0.21.0; a command-scoped GOPROXY mirror was needed when proxy.golang.org timed out. An initial local Python Jsonnet build could not find Python3.14 headers and was abandoned without global changes.

Download profile.schema.json, storage.schema.json, storage.model.schema.json and iscsi.schema.json from [Agama commit6d218f662791a49c7ded902da619558448ef08b8](https://github.com/agama-project/agama/tree/6d218f662791a49c7ded902da619558448ef08b8/rust/agama-lib/share) into an ignored directory. Run Jsonnet on answers/agama-uefi.golden, then native_validate.py with that resulting JSON path and the schema directory. The helper verifies pinned source hashes before local-only reference resolution. It also parses answers/autoinstall-uefi.golden with PyYAML. This confirms syntax/schema/selected values for those pinned tools, not real ISO compatibility.
